items.title: Santo Pecora Interview, 1972-11-09
items.q: Well, Johnny Lala didn't play with the Italian band, no.

ctx.x: The guys that played in that band... Tony Perrani and I was the only one that got to be known, you know, to go out of town. Yeah.
I'm trying to think of the guys from the French Quarter then. Who was that? Johnny Lala was around? Was he with you to? Well, Johnny Lala didn't play with the Italian band, no.
He played with just like Valley Hoon, dances and all that stuff. Yeah. He played with Schilling band for a long time.

items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1958-09-24
items.q: So I brought him up there and had to rehearse him and everything. And had a trombone player there. Santa sat in, played a couple of numbers. Man, right away this meeting wanted Santa.

ctx.x: I was a booking agent. He had a lot of them, yeah.

So I brought him up there and had to rehearse him and everything. And had a trombone player there. Santa sat in, played a couple of numbers. Man, right away this meeting wanted Santa. Took 15 trombone players. Then five though. Put him on the netted job. So we were working there. We'd go to work at 8 o'clock. To one. Five hours. To the peak north. We'd go to work at 8 o'clock. To one. Five hours. To the peak north. We'd go to about 13 men, 12, 13 men. And after one o'clock. They keep a Dixieland combination. Wow.…
We stayed. That's what happened. When was that? Was that after, quite a while after Tom Brown and the. Oh, Tom Brown. Yeah. He'd been up there and back.

items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: First he comes to work and we're getting $125 a piece, $250 of brass to him, him and I.

ctx.x: No, no, no, no, no, no.

That was all by booking agent by, you know? That goes by my ugly, suspicious mindless dear. So finally what happened, I said to him, he said, well, I can play so-and-so some ways. He won't be out of a job. He leaves tonight, he goes and we'll wait tomorrow night. So they asked him and so they said, you know, them boys work together. The only thing I worked with him, I had him bone for me when he was running, but I thought he had to work. First he comes to work and we're getting $125 a piece, $250 of brass to him,…

Yeah, I don't know. None of us know him. Oh, you don't know him. I mean, we know him, but we don't play with him. Bill's a trombone player. I'm a schoolteacher. I know, but the trouble is true. Raymond's a book salesman.
